name: Trump Media & Technology Group

summary.text: Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. (Nasdaq: DJT), operator of Truth Social, became a public company on March 25, 2024 through a business combination with the special-purpose acquisition company Digital World Acquisition Corp.; Devin Nunes is chief executive. Donald Trump was its largest shareholder and in December 2024 transferred all 114,750,000 of his shares, about 53 percent of the company, to the Donald J. Trump Revocable Trust, of which he is sole beneficiary and Donald Trump Jr. sole trustee. In 2025 the company raised about $2.5 billion in a private placement to fund a bitcoin treasury and reported holdings of about $2 billion in bitcoin and bitcoin-related securities by July 2025.

facts.claim: Digital World Acquisition Corp. shareholders approved the merger with Trump Media & Technology Group on March 22, 2024; the business combination closed on March 25, 2024, with the combined company operating as Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. and its common stock and warrants listed on Nasdaq as DJT and DJTWW from March 26, 2024. The deal had been announced in October 2021 and delayed for more than two years amid regulatory scrutiny and legal disputes.
facts.quote: Digital World now operates as "Trump Media & Technology Group Corp." following the successful completion of the Business Combination.

facts.claim: At the merger's close Trump held a stake reported at up to 69 percent depending on DWAC shareholder redemptions, and was barred by the merger terms from selling his shares for six months.
facts.quote: That represents as much as a 69% stake in the company depending on the rate of share redemptions by DWAC shareholders.

sources.title: Trump Media stock ticker DJT debuts after DWAC merger

facts.claim: On December 17, 2024, Trump transferred all 114,750,000 of his Trump Media shares, about 53 percent of the company's outstanding stock, to the Donald J. Trump Revocable Trust, of which he is sole beneficiary; SEC filings showed he received no payment and that Donald Trump Jr., as sole trustee, holds sole voting and investment power. Trump's Office of Government Ethics Form 278e records the transfer as neither a purchase nor a sale.
facts.quote: Trump did not receive any money for the gift of the 114,750,000 shares to the Donald J. Trump Revocable Trust on Tuesday, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

facts.claim: On March 24, 2025, Trump Media announced a non-binding agreement with Crypto.com to launch exchange-traded funds and products under its Truth.Fi fintech brand; on April 22, 2025 it said it had signed a binding agreement with Crypto.com and Yorkville America Digital, with Crypto.com to provide back-end technology, custody and cryptocurrencies for the ETFs.
facts.quote: Trump Media said on April 22 that it signed a binding agreement with Crypto.com and asset manager Yorkville America Digital to launch ETFs

facts.claim: In May 2025 Trump Media entered subscription agreements with about 50 institutional investors for a private placement of 55,857,181 common shares at $25.72 and $1.0 billion of 0.00% convertible senior secured notes due 2028, for net proceeds of about $2.32 billion earmarked for a bitcoin treasury and general corporate purposes, according to the company's Form 8-K.

facts.claim: On July 21, 2025, Trump Media announced in a Form 8-K exhibit that it had accumulated approximately $2 billion in bitcoin and bitcoin-related securities, about two-thirds of its roughly $3 billion in liquid assets, and had allocated about $300 million to an options strategy for bitcoin-related securities. CEO Devin Nunes said the assets 'help ensure our Company's financial freedom, help protect us against discrimination by financial institutions'.
facts.quote: Those holdings comprise around two-thirds of Trump Media's approximately $3 billion in liquid assets.

facts.claim: An April 2025 SEC resale registration listed more than 134 million shares that could be sold by Trump and other holders, including a Cayman Islands-based entity, YA II PN Ltd; the filing concerned potential resales, and no foreign sovereign investor in Trump Media was identified in the sources reached.
facts.quote: All told, Trump Media could sell off more than 134 million shares by Trump and other shareholders including a Cayman Islands-based group called YA II PN LTD.
